svg.text: Smart Elevator: full architecture (dispatcher + both cars)
2 cars, 8 floors. Every 8-bit "floor vector" has one bit per floor: bit k stands for floor k. Blue wires belong to Car A, magenta wires to Car B.
Hall buttons (UP / DOWN at each floor)
8 UP buttons + 8 DOWN buttons, one bit per floor
clk and rst go to every register in all three blocks
(dispatcher, Car A and Car B all update on the same rising clock edge)
has no logic of its own: it only wires the dispatcher (u_dispatch) and the two cars (u_car0, u_car1) together
picks which car answers each call
assigned: already given to a car
separate UP and DOWN sets, 8 bits each
free calls = pending AND NOT assigned
calls that are waiting but not yet given to any car
lowest floor with a free UP call
lowest floor with a free DOWN call
gives: the chosen floor · is it an UP or DOWN call · is there any call at all
floor vector (all zeros if no call)
mark the chosen floor as assigned
yes → Car B, no or tie → Car A
Next register values (stored on the next clock edge)
answered = answered by Car A OR answered by Car B
pending ← (pending OR new button press) AND NOT answered
assigned ← (assigned AND NOT answered) OR new assignment
owner ← the nearer car, for the new assignment
this wiring is everything elevator_coordinator.v contains
Dispatcher → Car A: the hall calls Car A must answer
Dispatcher → Car B: the hall calls Car B must answer
Car A → Dispatcher: where it is, which calls it answered
Car B → Dispatcher: where it is, which calls it answered
Buttons in: from the top-level input ports
next_dir0 / next_dir1 are also wired out of each car, only so the website can show them.

signal inside one block / shared input
Short names you will see in the Verilog code

pend = pending · asgd = assigned · asg = assigned calls · up / dn = up / down · btn = button · dir = direction · dist = distance · serve = calls answered · targets = target floors · here = current floor as a one-hot vector
enc = encoder · dec = decoder · d0 / d1 = distance for car 0 / car 1 · 0 / 1 at the end of a name = Car A / Car B · u_ = instance (one placed copy of a module) · clk = clock · rst = reset
posedge = rising (positive) clock edge · FSM = finite state machine · states in code: IDLE, MOVE_UP = moving up, MOVE_DN = moving down, DOOR = door open · reg = register · FF = flip-flop
